## Summary

`tests/interfaces/store/test_reads_under_sync_contention.py:152` bounds each `_rebar_cli` read
at `timeout=10` while a background thread holds the tracker write lock. It is the same construct
as `dire-negative-bunting` — a wall-clock bound doing duty as a behavioural oracle — with even
thinner headroom, and it has NOT yet been observed failing.

## Why it is a sibling, and why it was NOT fixed in the same change

Same shape: hold the writer lock, run a read through the real CLI in a subprocess, and use the
elapsed time to decide whether the read stalled. Its blocking signature is ~120s
(`release.wait(timeout=120)`), so the bound discriminates in principle.

But the semantics DIFFER, which is why this is not a mechanical copy of that fix. Its docstring
states the product contract it is checking: 'each read waits <=2s for the lock then serves its
local snapshot'. So `timeout=10` is testing a real 2s product deadline plus overhead — not merely
liveness. Raising it the way `dire-negative-bunting` was raised would weaken a genuine product
assertion. The right remedy needs a decision about how much of that 10s is the 2s guarantee and
how much is machine slack, and that is a different judgement from the one already made.

## Additional exposure

The call sits inside a `for name, argv, shape, complete in SURFACES` loop, so several subprocess
invocations run under one held lock. Cumulative slowness on a constrained runner therefore has
more chances to cross the bound than the single-call case that already failed.

## Evidence from the sibling investigation

On this machine (load 9.9) the analogous preview read completed in ~1.2s with the writer lock
held. The failing sibling case crossed 15s on a macOS CI runner — a >12x excursion. A 10s bound
over a documented 2s target is 5x, i.e. thinner than the one that already broke.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Decide, and record, how the 10s splits between the 2s product deadline and machine slack.
- [ ] The bound tolerates a CI-scale slowdown without weakening the <=2s guarantee — e.g. assert
      the product deadline separately from the subprocess liveness bound, rather than conflating
      them in one number.
- [ ] The test still fails if a read genuinely stalls on the held lock (mutation-check it).
- [ ] The per-surface loop's cumulative exposure is considered, not just the single-call case.

## Found by

The Step 7 construct sweep while fixing `dire-negative-bunting`. Not observed failing; filed
rather than fixed so the product-deadline question gets a deliberate answer.
